sources.content: RFC 0019: streaming server rendering in Ixtolen. Motivation: Ixtolen pages render the full HTML before sending any byte, so a page with one slow data call holds back the whole response. On the docs site the median time to first byte is 820 milliseconds. This RFC lets a route send its layout at once and stream slow sections later. A section opts in by wrapping its content in a `<Deferred>` component with a `fallback` prop. Routes without any `<Deferred>` behave exactly as today.

Limits and rollout. A deferred section that does not resolve within 10 seconds renders its fallback and logs a warning. Streaming is turned off for requests from known crawlers, which get the full page in one response. Response headers, including cookies, must be set before the first byte, so a deferred section cannot set cookies. The feature ships as experimental in version 3.4 behind `experimental.streaming: true` in `ixtolen.config.ts`, and becomes stable in 4.0 if no blocking bugs remain.

claims.text: A deferred Ixtolen section that does not resolve within 30 seconds renders its fallback.
Ixtolen routes without a Deferred component behave as they do today.
Known crawlers receive the full Ixtolen page in one response.
Streaming ships as experimental in Ixtolen version 3.4.
The median time to first byte on the Ixtolen docs site is 820 milliseconds.
Deferred Ixtolen sections can set cookies.
